title: Experiment readiness rubric and oncall cadence notes
content:
Purpose: working checklist and lightweight rubric we can gate on before starting canary/AB exposures for LLM-backend changes. Focus: cross-functional readiness (prod observability, ops cadence, rollback, experiment definition). Use this as a pre-flight for any incremental exposure where model behavior or routing may cause user-visible regressions.

High-level run phases (proposal):
- PREP: engineering + product + SRE agree on metrics, thresholds, rollback triggers, and communication plan.
- CANARY: 0.5% -> 5% traffic in micro-slices with strict SLO monitoring.
- STABLE EXPANSION: 5% -> 25% with secondary signals monitored.
- RAMP / GA: progressive until full rollout with automated checks and manual sign-off.

Readiness rubric (gate MUST be green or explicitly risk-accepted):
1) Metrics + Instrumentation (owner: eng lead)
   - Primary user-facing metrics defined and instrumented (examples: median latency, p95 latency, tokens/sec, error rate, hallucination flag rate, downstream API failures).
   - Dashboards exist and are accessible to oncall and PMs (link to dashboard in linked_artifacts).
   - Synthetic smoke tests created to exercise hot paths (short prompts, long prompts, function calls).

2) SLAs & thresholds (owner: SRE)
   - Pre-defined thresholds: p95 latency increase <= 20% over baseline OR absolute p95 < 600ms (whichever is stricter).
   - Error rate increase <= 0.5 ppts absolute.
   - Note: for cost/throughput experiments we add cost-per-1k-tokens target.

3) Data quality & safety signals (owner: applied-ml)
   - Prompt suite for regression checks (10–20 prompts covering edge cases).
   - Toxicity / hallucination heuristics wired to alerting.
   - Quick evaluation harness (local/CI) with baseline scoring.

4) Fallback plan & automated revert (owner: infra)
   - Canary routing supports immediate 100% re-route to fallback model within 60s.
   - Feature flag / config toggle exists to flip rollout off programmatically.
   - Revert playbook excerpt included in runbook.

5) Communication & stakeholder alignment (owner: PM)
   - Slack channel and pager roster announced at least 24h before start.
   - List of stakeholders and primary contacts for legal/security/customer success.
   - Customer-impact list (who to notify if degraded).

Operational oncall cadence (proposal):
- Pre-launch: daily quick-sync 09:30 (15m) with eng, sres, applied-ml, pm for first 72h of canary.
- Canary: dedicated pager rotation for experiment (one SRE, one eng lead) 24/7 for first 48h, then 12/7 for next 5 days.
- Escalation ladder: pager -> eng lead -> srep -> oncall SRE manager. Rapid meeting cadence if any threshold breached.

Roles & responsibilities (short):
- Experiment owner (PM): approves go/no-go and stakeholder comms.
- Eng owner: implements routing, fallback, and metrics.
- SRE owner: sets alerts, dashboards, rollback automation.
- Applied-ML owner: evals & safety signals.

Observability checklist (pre-canary):
- Dashboards: latency, errors, tokens per request, model selection counts.
- Alerting: p95 or error thresholds, regression scoring increase >5%.
- Traces: end-to-end traces that show routing decision & model variant.
- Cost telemetry: token-aggregates and variant-level cost estimates.

Example slice plan (micro-cohorts):
- Slice A: internal beta users (10% of canary) - lowest risk, highest visibility.
- Slice B: random new users (30% of canary) - representative traffic.
- Slice C: paid customers w/ low-fraction exposure (60% of canary) - notify CS.

Statistical note for A/B:
- Typical min sample for signal evaluation: at least 5k impressions per variant or use sequential testing. Power calculations live in Confluence; for quick checks we use approximate significance with Bonferroni-corrected p < 0.05. Avoid declaring wins in first 24h.

Rollback criteria (auto + manual):
- Auto-revert triggers: p95 latency > threshold for 5m AND error rate spike > 1ppt sustained 3m OR safety-score degradation > 10% on regression suite.
- Manual-revert criteria: any customer-impacting behavior reported by CS or legal required action.

Quick revert procedure (playbook):
1) Flip feature flag to route 100% traffic to previous model.
2) Notify #rollouts with reason & incident stub.
3) Open JIRA with incident template and assign SRE/eng.
4) Run post-mortem + safety fixes before next attempt.

Pre-flight checklist (tick before kickoff):
- [ ] Metrics + dashboards reviewed by SRE + eng owner
- [ ] Regression suite result baseline attached to ticket
- [ ] Fallback toggle tested in staging (end-to-end)
- [ ] Pager roster assigned and Slack channel created
- [ ] PM approved communication plan to CS and partners
- [ ] Legal/privacy checklist (if any PII changes)

Open questions / notes-to-self:
- Consider adding a short-lived 'experiment health annoucements' bot message template for #rollouts to reduce noise.
- Decision: how long to keep canary traces (cost vs debugging needs) — default 7 days.
- Need a small library of synthetic prompts for multi-lingual models; ask LA team to contribute.

References and quick links included above.

Next steps: iterate this rubric with SRE and applied-ML in the next rollout guild sync (scheduled 2025-02-20). If comfortable, adopt as the default pre-flight checklist for all model & routing rollouts.

Notes to reviewer: this doc is intentionally concise; please add missing metrics or thresholds you care about and tag owners inline.
